page: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance runs on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with x86_64 architecture operating at up to 3.9 GHz. It features 48 physical cores and 96 dedicated vCPUs with hyperthreading enabled, supplemented by a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It includes 384.0 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle dedicated GPUs, but it integrates 5,700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight strong throughput across multi-threaded and memory-intensive evaluations. The instance scored 22,208.0 in Geekbench multi-core and 107,119.74 in the PassMark CPU assessment, ranking in the top tier. Extended instruction performance is bolstered by instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, achieving 133,972.38 in PassMark CPU extended tests. Memory subsystem testing reflects top-tier bandwidth, delivering 385.12 GB/sec on large read blocks and caching bandwidth of 7,680.87 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core metrics display middle-to-strong levels, with stress-ng single-core recording an average 2,120.69 and Geekbench single-core at 2,191.0.

Data handling benchmarks show exceptional performance in memory-bound and storage-adjacent scenarios. The server achieved 169.45 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads and scored 34,128.53 in PassMark database operations, placing it in the top tier. In CPU-based LLM inference, it delivers top-tier prompt processing throughput across small, medium, and large models (e.g., 4,292.93 tokens/sec on 135M and 41.0 tokens/sec on 70B models), though text generation throughput remains at average-to-strong levels due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware.

AWS m8id.24xlarge presents an efficient profile for large-scale operations requiring both high compute parallelization and rapid local ephemeral storage. By eliminating external network disk overhead for scratch spaces via the 5,700 GB NVMe SSD volume, it is well suited for high-throughput relational and NoSQL databases, large code compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, and CPU-driven vector operations.
